rulings.docket_item: Adopt or decline the proposed re-span of Jer.3.11-Jer.3.20 at Jer.3.14 (peer PROPOSAL; boss adoption required).
rulings.grounds: DECLINED; the disclosure and splice cures stand as author work. The proposal turns on a fresh plural addressee at Jer.3.14. The address-marker half of that test does hold there: שׁ֣וּבוּ בָנִ֤ים שׁוֹבָבִים֙ (oshb:Jer.3.14, byte tier) is an imperative carrying its own vocative. The freshness half fails on the bytes, and it is decisive. The second person plural is already standing inside the very verse that opens this unit's invitation, לֽוֹא אַפִּ֥יל פָּנַ֖י בָּכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.3.12, byte tier), and again at the close of the next verse, וּבְקוֹלִ֥י לֹא שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם (oshb:Jer.3.13, byte tier), against the singular imperative with its vocative in the first of those verses, שׁ֣וּבָה מְשֻׁבָ֤ה יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ (oshb:Jer.3.12, byte tier), and the feminine singular imperative and suffix opening the second, אַ֚ךְ דְּעִ֣י עֲוֺנֵ֔ךְ (oshb:Jer.3.13, byte tier). The second person therefore alternates between singular and plural inside oshb:Jer.3.12 and again inside oshb:Jer.3.13, two verses and one verse before the proposed seam. The plural addressee at oshb:Jer.3.14 is RESUMED, not opened - a byte-true device straddling the proposed seam, which argues continuity against the cut. The number is carried by the pointed bytes alone; the second witness renders all five sites number-blind, and its rendering is tier-4 and never evidence in either direction. The row's remaining negative term holds: no word-event formula, koh-amar onset or messenger-formula onset falls inside Jer.3.11-Jer.3.20 (byte read of all ten verses), so no tier-1 onset class is available at Jer.3.14 to carry the cut on its own. The parashah layer supplies nothing at the proposed seam in either direction: the chapter's segs stand at MT 3:5 (PE), MT 3:10 (PE), MT 3:17 (SAMEKH) and MT 3:25 (SAMEKH) (inventory: 4 marked verses in the chapter, 0 at MT 3:13), single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets, PE not conflated with SAMEKH, and absence is never counterevidence. CONTROLLING OBJECT NAMED: the docket's grounds place the earliest second person plural of the span at וּבְקוֹלִ֥י לֹא שְׁמַעְתֶּ֖ם (oshb:Jer.3.13); the bytes place it one verse earlier at לֽוֹא אַפִּ֥יל פָּנַ֖י בָּכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.3.12). The controlling object is the earliest second-person-plural FORM inside Jer.3.11-Jer.3.20, and its site is oshb:Jer.3.12.

(2) The disposition that keeps the imperative-with-vocative at oshb:Jer.3.14 inside the unit must rest on that resumption, not on the absence of a formula. rulings.docket_item: Adopt or decline the proposed cut at Jer.4.7 splitting the lion/destroyer description out of Jer.4.5-Jer.4.9 (peer PROPOSAL).
rulings.grounds: DECLINED. Jer.4.7 carries no vocative, no imperative and no second-person verb (byte read of the whole verse). Its only second-person material is a pair of possessive suffixes inside a purpose clause governed by a third-person subject, לָשׂ֤וּם אַרְצֵךְ֙ לְשַׁמָּ֔ה עָרַ֥יִךְ (oshb:Jer.4.7, byte tier), where the final kaf is consonantally certain against the mem a plural possessor would carry. A possessive suffix is a referential turn, not an address, so the ruled explicit-addressee-shift class does not engage on its address-marker half. Its freshness half fails too: the plural summons that opens this unit, הַגִּ֣ידוּ בִֽיהוּדָ֗ה וּבִירוּשָׁלִַ֨ם֙ הַשְׁמִ֔יעוּ (oshb:Jer.4.5, byte tier), RESUMES immediately on the far side of the proposed seam with three further plural imperatives, חִגְר֥וּ שַׂקִּ֖ים סִפְד֣וּ וְהֵילִ֑ילוּ (oshb:Jer.4.8, byte tier), so Jer.4.7 stands enclosed inside one continuous discourse-frame imperative address rather than opening a fresh one. The formula half of the row's own denial is byte-true and the docket says so: no onset formula stands at Jer.4.7. With the address half corrected the verse still meets no tier-1 onset class - not a koh-amar onset with a frame-owner change, not a discourse-frame imperative, not a date-formula onset, not a vision-report opening, not an explicit addressee shift. The docket's finding about the speaking VOICE is upheld and is not disturbed here: the voice does move, from divine first person at oshb:Jer.4.6 through third-person description to a first-person-plural speaker naming YHWH in the third person at oshb:Jer.4.8. But a speaker turn is not one of the ruled cut classes, and it is not even co-sited with the proposed seam - it lands one verse later, inside the resumed imperative. The parashah layer offers no corroboration at the proposed seam: the chapter's segs stand as SAMEKH at MT 4:2, MT 4:18, MT 4:21 and MT 4:26 and as PE at MT 4:8 and MT 4:31 (inventory: 6 marked verses in the chapter, 0 at MT 4:6), the two types kept apart, single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets, and absence is never counterevidence.

(2) The re-argued strongest_rejected_alternative must rest on the RESUMPTION of the plural summons at חִגְר֥וּ שַׂקִּ֖ים סִפְד֣וּ וְהֵילִ֑ילוּ (oshb:Jer.4.8, byte tier), which encloses Jer.4.7 inside one continuous address, and on the absence of any tier-1 onset class at that verse - not on the absence of an imperative, vocative or messenger formula alone. The field stays at one sentence plus the mandated rival-disclosure sentence. (3) web:Jer.4.8 is inside this row's own span, so no refs-mirror entry is owed for the new ground.

rulings.docket_item: Adopt or decline the proposed cut at Jer.4.31 separating the death-cry from the koh-amar-opened oracle of Jer.4.27-Jer.4.31 (peer PROPOSAL flagged for boss adoption).
rulings.grounds: DECLINED. The proposed seam falls at a verse whose FIRST word is a subordinating causal connective: כִּי֩ ק֨וֹל כְּחוֹלָ֜ה שָׁמַ֗עְתִּי (oshb:Jer.4.31, byte tier) - the connective binds the death-cry back to the verse before it, and nothing at that site belongs to a ruled tier-1 onset class. The onset shape is a first-person perception verb. It is not a koh-amar onset with a frame-owner change, not a date-formula onset, not a vision-report opening, not a discourse-frame imperative, and not an explicit addressee shift - Jer.4.31 addresses no one, carrying no vocative, no imperative and no second-person form of any kind (byte read of the whole verse), and the daughter-of-Zion cry inside it is reported in the third person before the quoted words. The docket's correction of the challengers' blended count object is upheld and re-derived here: the three comparanda they invoke are byte-distinct shapes - a speech-attribution finite verb (oshb:Jer.4.10; oshb:Jer.5.4), an exclamatory outcry (oshb:Jer.4.19) and a verse-initial vocative to the deity (oshb:Jer.5.3) - and none of them is a perception verb; further, the perception form inside oshb:Jer.4.19 itself stands under a ketiv/qere note (inventory: 2 notes at MT 4:19, one of the twelve doubled-note verses, single-witness), so the read text there is not a first-person perception form at all. The parashah layer corroborates the EXISTING close rather than the proposed cut: the chapter's PE is keyed at MT 4:31, and under the follow-the-verse keying re-derived here from the inventory - at the eleven parent-frame seams the frame-final verse carries a seg 11 of 11 (MT 1:3, 6:30, 10:25, 17:27, 20:18, 24:10, 29:32, 33:26, 39:18, 45:5, 51:64) and the frame-initial verse 0 of 11 - that seg stands AFTER MT 4:31, at this row's own back seam. It is single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets, PE not conflated with SAMEKH, cited as corroboration only and never as the ground.

rulings.docket_item: Rule whether Jer.6.8 is cut into its own row out of Jer.6.6-Jer.6.8 (peer: NOT ordered, explicit boss adoption required).
rulings.grounds: ADOPTED. Both halves of the ruled explicit-addressee-shift class hold at Jer.6.8, and the ground the row gives for refusing the cut is byte-false. Inside oshb:Jer.6.6 the reported divine speech commands the besiegers in the plural, כִּרְת֣וּ עֵצָ֔ה וְשִׁפְכ֥וּ עַל יְרוּשָׁלִַ֖ם סֹלְלָ֑ה (oshb:Jer.6.6, byte tier), and speaks OF the city in the third person, הִ֚יא הָעִ֣יר הָפְקַ֔ד כֻּלָּ֖הּ עֹ֥שֶׁק בְּקִרְבָּֽהּ (oshb:Jer.6.6, byte tier); oshb:Jer.6.7 continues third-person of her, יִשָּׁ֨מַע בָּ֧הּ עַל פָּנַ֛י (oshb:Jer.6.7, byte tier). At oshb:Jer.6.8 the city becomes the party addressed: הִוָּסְרִי֙ יְר֣וּשָׁלִַ֔ם פֶּן תֵּקַ֥ע נַפְשִׁ֖י מִמֵּ֑ךְ (oshb:Jer.6.8, byte tier) and פֶּן אֲשִׂימֵ֣ךְ שְׁמָמָ֔ה (oshb:Jer.6.8, byte tier) - an imperative carrying the city as its own vocative, with two second-person feminine-singular suffixes whose final kaf is consonantally certain against the five third-person feminine singular suffix forms carried across the two preceding verses; the second witness renders it as direct address, “Be instructed, Jerusalem” (web:Jer.6.8). The address-marker half holds, since the shift is carried by a vocative and an imperative and not by a bare suffix. The freshness half holds too: no second-person feminine form stands anywhere in Jer.6.6-Jer.6.7 (byte read of both verses), and the plural addressee of oshb:Jer.6.6 does not resume after Jer.6.8, since oshb:Jer.6.9 opens its own bare koh-amar on a fresh topic and addresses a masculine singular. No backward-binding connective stands at Jer.6.8. The ruled granularity licenses a cut on an explicit addressee shift independently of any formula, and the corpus already installs exactly that seam at Jer.6.18 on the identical warrant, so declining here would apply one criterion two ways. The only ground left for the present span is the Masoretic bracket - SAMEKH keyed at MT 6:5 and PE keyed at MT 6:8 (inventory; single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets, PE not conflated with SAMEKH) - and a tier-3-only ground is insufficient in a ruling exactly as it is in a challenge or a defense. Frame law satisfied: both resulting rows sit wholly inside M1 Jer.1.4-Jer.6.30 and no frame seam is straddled.

rulings.docket_item: Rule the 6:19/6:20 boundary question inside Jer.6.18-Jer.6.20: adopt an exact re-cut there, or decline (any re-cut is a PROPOSAL requiring explicit adoption).
rulings.grounds: DECLINED; no re-cut is adopted at 6:19/6:20. The docket's byte finding is upheld - a second-person turn does fall at Jer.6.20 - but it is not of the class that cuts, on either half of the test, and naming the objects dissolves the inconsistency complaint. Address-marker half: this row's front seam is cut on imperatives carrying their own vocatives, שִׁמְע֣וּ הַגּוֹיִ֑ם וּדְעִ֥י עֵדָ֖ה (oshb:Jer.6.18, byte tier) and שִׁמְעִ֣י הָאָ֔רֶץ (oshb:Jer.6.19, byte tier), whereas Jer.6.20 carries no vocative, no imperative and no second-person verb (byte read of the whole verse) - only two possessive suffixes inside a rhetorical question, עֹלֽוֹתֵיכֶם֙ לֹ֣א לְרָצ֔וֹן וְזִבְחֵיכֶ֖ם (oshb:Jer.6.20, byte tier). Those are byte-distinct objects: the controlling object for the seam criterion is an explicit address marker, a vocative or a second-person verb form, not a second-person suffix; so the criterion is applied once, not two ways. Freshness half: the plural possessors at Jer.6.20 are not fresh. The same second-person plural addressee already stands two and three verses back, at וּמִצְא֥וּ מַרְגּ֖וֹעַ לְנַפְשְׁכֶ֑ם (oshb:Jer.6.16, byte tier) and וַהֲקִמֹתִ֤י עֲלֵיכֶם֙ צֹפִ֔ים (oshb:Jer.6.17, byte tier), inside the preceding unit, so Jer.6.20 RESUMES the address to the people that the witness-summons of Jer.6.18-Jer.6.19 interrupted; it does not open one. That resumption, and not the shared indictment content, is what actually holds the verse inside this unit. The parashah layer corroborates neither seam: under the follow-the-verse keying re-derived here from the inventory (frame-final verse carries a seg 11 of 11 at the eleven parent-frame seams, frame-initial 0 of 11), the chapter's SAMEKH keyed at MT 6:15 and MT 6:20 stand at the Jer.6.15|Jer.6.16 and Jer.6.20|Jer.6.21 seams, bracketing Jer.6.16-Jer.6.20 ACROSS both rows; the inventory records 0 segs at MT 6:19 and absence is never counterevidence; single-witness, tier-3, non-driving throughout.

rulings.grounds: ADOPTED, inside the book's single offset zone, every ref dual-cited. The row's present front seam stands on no ruled tier-1 class and is contradicted by a byte-true device straddling it, while two ruled classes converge one verse later. At oshb:Jer.9.1 = web:Jer.9.2 the first-person wish closes on a causal clause in third-person plural description, כִּ֤י כֻלָּם֙ מְנָ֣אֲפִ֔ים עֲצֶ֖רֶת בֹּגְדִֽים (oshb:Jer.9.1 = web:Jer.9.2, byte tier), and the row's own opening word carries the same third-person plural subject forward under a consecutive prefix form, וַֽיַּדְרְכ֤וּ אֶת לְשׁוֹנָם֙ קַשְׁתָּ֣ם שֶׁ֔קֶר (oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3, byte tier) - a byte-true device straddling this row's own front seam, which argues continuity against the cut and is disclosed in no field. A turn to third-person description is in any case not one of the ruled tier-1 onset classes. At the proposed seam two of them converge: אִ֤ישׁ מֵרֵעֵ֨הוּ֙ הִשָּׁמֵ֔רוּ וְעַל כָּל אָ֖ח אַל תִּבְטָ֑חוּ (oshb:Jer.9.3 = web:Jer.9.4, byte tier) is a plural imperative followed by a plural prohibitive - the ruled discourse-frame-imperative class, rendered as direct address by the second witness, “Everyone beware of his neighbor, and don't trust in any brother” (web:Jer.9.4) - and it is at the same time an explicit addressee shift on both halves of that test, since the three verses before the adopted seam, oshb:Jer.8.23-Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.1-Jer.9.3, carry no second-person form of any kind (byte read of all three verses), so the addressee is both explicitly marked and fresh. The neum-YHWH tag closing oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3, נְאֻם יְהוָֽה (oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3, byte tier), is licensed closure corroboration exactly here and only here: under the ruled law it closes a unit only where a fresh tier-1 onset follows, and at the present seam none does. Tier-3 corroboration coincides without driving: under the follow-the-verse keying re-derived here from the inventory - at the eleven parent-frame seams the frame-final verse carries a seg 11 of 11 (MT 1:3, 6:30, 10:25, 17:27, 20:18, 24:10, 29:32, 33:26, 39:18, 45:5, 51:64) and the frame-initial verse 0 of 11 - the SAMEKH keyed at oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3 stands AFTER that verse, which is to say at the adopted seam, and the SAMEKH keyed at oshb:Jer.9.5 = web:Jer.9.6 stands at the receiving row's unchanged back seam; both are SAMEKH, no PE is in play, single-witness, tier-3 weak in the Prophets, non-driving. Frame law satisfied: both rows remain wholly inside M2 Jer.7.1-Jer.10.25. HELD-OPEN CONSTRAINT, binding on the execution: this ruling moves a seam on addressee-onset and cohesion grounds only. It does NOT assign the speaking voice of the lament, which stays held open, and the neum-YHWH tag at oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3 may not be used to assign a speaker to the verses standing before it.

(2) P03-008: span field; boundary_rationale fully re-authored on the adopted onset, אִ֤ישׁ מֵרֵעֵ֨הוּ֙ הִשָּׁמֵ֔רוּ וְעַל כָּל אָ֖ח אַל תִּבְטָ֑חוּ (oshb:Jer.9.3 = web:Jer.9.4, byte tier), with the close unchanged at oshb:Jer.9.5 = web:Jer.9.6 before the title-stack koh-amar onset לָכֵ֗ן כֹּ֤ה אָמַר֙ יְהוָ֣ה צְבָא֔וֹת (oshb:Jer.9.6 = web:Jer.9.7, byte tier); the retired third-person-description warrant is struck. (3) P03-009 (Jer.9.7-Jer.9.11 (WEB) = oshb:Jer.9.6-Jer.9.10): NO span edit and NO seam edit - its front-seam corroboration, the SAMEKH keyed at oshb:Jer.9.5 = web:Jer.9.6, is unchanged and stays true, and its ketiv/qere disclosure at oshb:Jer.9.7 = web:Jer.9.8 (inventory: 1 note, the zone's only one, single-witness) is unchanged. SUPERSESSION: the docket's remedy arm (2) for P03-008 - stop presenting the seg at oshb:Jer.9.2 = web:Jer.9.3 as the opening mark, say instead that it stands inside the span and that the front seam carries no seg - is SUPERSEDED, because after the respan that seg stands AT the front seam. CORPUS-SCOPED ORDER, EXPLICITLY SWEEP-SCOPED AND NOT FOLDED INTO THIS RESPAN: the docket's arm (4), bare in-zone chapter.verse coordinates in row prose, is the class the docket records recurring at P03-010, P03-011 and P03-013; it remains its OWN sweep over every row touching web ch 9 or oshb:Jer.8.23 / oshb ch 9, and the qualifiers ordered above for P03-007 and P03-008 are only the two rows this respan re-authors and do not discharge that sweep.
